notes:
## Millstrand lazy reads and telemetry (read-only exploration, 2026-10-08)

### Findings

- `server/index.ts` routes `/api/board` to `StrandData.board()` and `/api/cards/:id` to `detail()`. The board is a summary projection from `server/workspace-database.ts` and `server/provenance.ts`: no card bodies or full notes; `StrandData.board()` sorts the card metadata and fails above 10,000 rows rather than truncating. There is no API pagination/cursor today. Card detail is fetched on selection via `strand kanban card`; full card notes, task notes, card graph, and dependency graph have separate endpoints. `server/strand.ts` caches/coalesces each endpoint read for three seconds. The persisted DB path is discovered once per 30-second window; SQL reads are read-only and report row count plus discovery/query/decode timing.
- Query demand lives in `src/lib/api/cards.ts`, hooks, and the poll owners. Board polls every 5s; selected card detail has no interval; notes poll every 5s only while the Notes tab is visible; graph polls every 10s for a selected graph; dependency reads poll only while graph nodes are expanded. `WorkspaceResourcePolls` is the single owner for workspace polls and disables log activity outside board/outline or selected issue/agent/run detail. Disabled readers share keys without starting fetches or timers. This is the strongest reusable idea: make demand visible at the query owner, then keep renderers as cache readers.
- Instrumentation is layered and injected: `shared/perf.ts` defines 5ms warn/50ms slow and `PerfLogger`; `server/index.ts` records HTTP method/path, elapsed time, status and bytes on finish/close; `server/strand.ts` times CLI calls with command target, workspace, output bytes and success/failure; `WorkspaceDatabase.readSnapshot()` records rows and discover/query/decode splits; `src/lib/api/transport.ts` logs browser fetch duration/status/bytes. Production server samples go to a rotating 5MiB `~/.local/state/millstrand-ui/perf.log`, with warn/slow tiers echoed to console. Constructors accept injected loggers; ordinary library use is silent.
- Correlation and client failure telemetry are limited. There is no request ID propagated from browser to server or subprocess. The route path and timestamps permit rough matching, but `commandTarget()` strips resource IDs. Browser transport records non-2xx responses after reading JSON, but a rejected `fetch()` or JSON parse fails before it records a sample. Server response logs retain status/bytes, while CLI/SQLite logs retain `outcome=failed` without the underlying failure text.
- `docs/read-performance.md` shows the diagnosis loop: use observed repeated slow samples, map them to an active poll owner and whether the surface needs the data, make the smallest query-demand or projection change, then verify request counts and rendered behavior against a real production server. Examples include a 1.94–2.01s `/api/agents` response (~658KB), repeated selected-card detail polls, and unnecessary log-activity polls on a bare Agents page; the recorded fixes removed unneeded polling or moved detail to demand.

### Hive MVP recommendation

Use the existing `@hive/shared` native Beads boundary (`lib/shared/src/bees-io.ts`: `beads()` and `showBead()`) with the selected `RepositoryEndpoint`; keep Hive’s Beads DB/native CLI as authority and parse spawn semantics once through `readSpawnRequest()` (`lib/shared/src/spawn-request.ts`). For the list surface, issue one filtered `br list --status open --label system --label bee --limit 50 --sort updated_at --reverse --json` call; `br list --help` confirms AND label filters and `--limit`/`--offset` pagination. Return a bounded page with an explicit next offset; do not use unlimited `--limit 0` in the UI. Fetch full `br show` data only for the selected spawn and any task detail the user opens, rather than doing per-row detail calls. Keep refreshing at one visible list owner and load details on selection.

For initial diagnosis, log one structured sample per HTTP request and native `br` call with request ID, command/filter, elapsed ms, result count/bytes, status/outcome and a concise error reason. Pass the same request ID to child-call samples; do not log descriptions, prompts, or dialogue contents. A short per-key in-flight/TTL cache can collapse overlapping polls; failed reads should remain visible and logged, never be converted to an empty board. Millstrand’s file rotation and multi-layer SQL timing are useful later if real measurements show the need, but are incidental complexity for the Hive POC.

Settled direction is reduced guidance/hook publication, local shared tracker operations during work, explicit startup/resume and final landing/handoff publication, and retained quality/data-safety checks. The user's exact wording was "they only need a sync on start of a worktree and perhaps before landing a PR"; final post-update handoff and the cross-clone qualification are the coordinator's supplied interpretation recorded on hv-szpc, not additional verbatim user statements.

Proposed smallest trigger ownership: let the agent workflow own one explicit beginning/resuming-work checkpoint, and make harness startup hooks environment-only. Session launch is not itself proof that new tracker work begins, and a single process cannot infer whether another agent already performed the logical checkpoint. Remove automatic full publication from session hooks and local-commit/pre-merge paths; keep lint-staged, typecheck, commitlint and visible environment/setup failures. Codex gets BEADS_DB from generated config already: remove a now purposeless Codex publication registration/branch rather than retain dead compatibility machinery. Single active clone means one selected SQLite tracker shared by concurrent local agents, not one agent. A local claim is immediately visible to those agents without a Git push. Another clone has independent SQLite: startup-only refresh plus delayed claim publication can allow overlapping work. If multiple clones are active, explicitly receive current state and publish claims before acting on them, treat claims as provisional until successful publication, and stop on disagreement without force/timestamp arbitration. This is best-effort coordination, not a global atomic lock; the existing publication lock is local. Do not silently promise cross-clone exclusivity.

Trade-offs and alternatives
Explicit workflow ownership removes duplicate hook/manual calls with no cache, sentinel, lease, polling or durable "already synced" state. The cost is reliance on agents following begin/resume and handoff guidance, and a longer remote visibility window. Keeping automatic startup plus deleting manual startup is possible, but has to prove successful coverage across harnesses/resumes and ad-hoc execution; it is less coherent with a work-boundary policy. Defining exactly once per worktree lifetime, or exactly two publications for every multi-bee run, would require new coordination assumptions not supplied here.
Leave the publisher's native JSONL safety, reconciliation, snapshot preservation, locking and failure propagation intact. Fewer caller checkpoints can reduce opportunities for churn but cannot promise a tracker commit count or prevent observation-only commits: every checkpoint publishes all pending shared tracker changes. title: Consult on Colony watchdog ownership
description: Read-only librarian consult. Parent hv-b10z: user asked to add persistent Colony health notification watchdog using mise.toml native [daemons.NAME], cc-notify. Independent watchdog polls public Colony status, notices failed colonies (even live daemon), sustained unavailability, deduplicates and reports recovery. No automatic wake/repair. Recommend narrow placement: Colony-owned monitor versus repo tooling; no code changes authorized by this consult. Also user correction to original suggestion of launchd: 'ok lets do that, check online and you'll see mise supports a deamon field directly'. Official https://mise.jdx.dev/daemons.html confirms top-level [daemons] via Pitchfork, installed mise 2026.10.4/pitchfork 2.29.0. Keep integration Mise-managed, not bespoke launchd. Return concise settled recommendation/evidence on this task; no documentation curation edits authorized.
notes:
Read-only consult delivery — 2026-10-08 — hv-b10z.1
Reviewed checkout bf9899cdbf2262a138e971ab02eccf615dad4f05; working tree initially clean. Own supplied claim verified as olive-positive-warbler, owner ct, linked from hv-savc; initial beads:sync succeeded. Scope: advice only, no application/document edits or changes to hv-b10z/hv-b10z.2.

1. Evidence and reuse
docs/architecture.md:9-16 assigns daemon ownership, supervision and private runtime persistence to Colony; Tooling owns repository maintenance. lib/colony/AGENTS.md preserves distinct CLI, server, colony-machine and supervisor lifetimes. GLOSSARY.md distinguishes the hosting daemon from each repository colony.
lib/shared/src/colony-protocol.ts:24-49 already exposes typed awake/asleep/failed colony states, repository root + Beads endpoint, and a failure message. Its status response includes every colony plus selected daemon socket/state. lib/colony/src/server.ts:97-109 and :373-400 publish that live view; lib/colony/src/colony.ts:40-57 makes pass failure a retained failed loop even while the server lives. Therefore PID checks or exit-code-only CLI checks miss the stated incident.
Reuse lib/colony/src/client.ts:33-55 requestServer(target, {kind: "status"}): public socket protocol, response parsing, state-selection check and 10-second request timeout already exist. This path never starts the daemon. The lazy-start path at :58-70 is separate and must not be used. lib/colony/README.md:223-239 documents sleep, temporary membership and explicit server selection.
The only supplied verbatim user correction is: "ok lets do that, check online and you'll see mise supports a deamon field directly". The remaining incident/request context comes from coordinator-authored hv-b10z and this task, not a directly inspected original transcript. I independently checked https://mise.jdx.dev/daemons.html: native [daemons.NAME] entries use run or task, with Mise providing configuration/environment and Pitchfork supervision. No existing cc-notify/watchdog integration found in lib/, .hive/, mise.toml or package.json. No historical evidence search or recurrence claim.

2. Recommendation
Colony owns health interpretation and notification policy; run it in an independent foreground process supervised by root mise.toml [daemons.colony-watchdog]. Proposed new files: lib/colony/src/watchdog.ts for polling/incident decisions and lib/colony/bin/watchdog.ts for executable composition. These are proposals, not existing mandatory file names. A Colony CLI subcommand is also acceptable if it reuses the same composition; a separate product or generic monitoring framework is unnecessary.
Use the existing read-only status client at the IO seam. Keep live socket reads, cc-notify subprocess invocation, clock/timer and local checkpoint IO injected from the executable. A small interface such as advanceWatchdog(previous, observation, now, policy) -> {next, notifications}, with a sequential runner applying effects, keeps decisions pure and restart behavior testable. Do not duplicate the wire schema, read the daemon database, infer health from spawn observations, or import scheduler/request internals. Keep imports within Colony plus @hive/shared; no new Shared behavior is needed.
Persist only watcher-owned notification bookkeeping in a separate local checkpoint: outage start and successfully delivered incident state, scoped to selected state/socket and repository root + Beads DB. This is not scheduler authority. Reuse server-selection semantics from bin/colony.ts:106-118; extract that existing helper locally only if a second entry requires it. Preserve --socket requiring --state.
Model daemon unavailability separately from per-colony failure. Failed colonies alert even on successful status responses; asleep is healthy. Preserve existing colony incidents while the daemon is unreachable. When reachability returns, clear the daemon outage and still report any failed colonies. A disappearing registration is not evidence that scheduling recovered. Deduplicate by incident identity, not daemon PID/instance ID or polling time. A successful notification precedes recording it delivered; failed notification delivery must remain visible and must not be marked sent.
Mise owns watcher process supervision/restart; the watcher owns observation and notification only. Do not make startup/readiness depend on a healthy Colony, declare a dependency that starts Colony, or call wake/add/repair. Configure the intended persistent lifecycle, not shell-leave auto-stop. Explicitly activate one selected checkout to avoid competing worktree watchers; retain that checkout until activation is moved.

3. Trade-offs
A Tooling script can technically consume the public CLI, but permanent Colony-state and recovery semantics are product behavior, so Tooling placement splits ownership and encourages either duplicated contracts or prohibited package imports. A daemon-internal notifier cannot observe daemon absence. A long-running Colony-owned executable reuses the existing public protocol with less process/JSON duplication than shelling out each poll. A CLI subprocess adapter remains valid if the implementation deliberately chooses that public seam and parses ok/kind/reason rather than text. Neither choice warrants moving monitor policy into Shared or broadening scheduler persistence.

4. Unresolved decisions / verification limits
Placement requires no further user decision. Poll interval, sustained-unavailability grace, changed-message re-alert policy and checkpoint pathname were not supplied as settled policy; the implementing agent should record explicit, modest defaults. There is no public fact distinguishing an intentional stopped daemon from an outage: while enabled, the monitor can treat sustained unreachability as unavailable; planned maintenance requires stopping the monitor unless a separate opt-out is explicitly desired. Do not invent a second desired-state registry.
Recovery language should distinguish reachable daemon, cleared colony failure and intentionally asleep colony; it cannot promise useful scheduling resumed merely because transport recovered. cc-notify plus a local checkpoint cannot promise exactly-once delivery across a crash between send and save; normal poll/restart deduplication is the scope.
No full quality/test suites, notification delivery, activation, boot behavior or implementation verification were run for this read-only consult. Existing code evidence supports ownership, not a completed watchdog.

- Interpretation: coordinator considered Colony monitor versus repository tooling and initially suggested launchd; user corrected the integration to native Mise daemons. Colony-owned independent monitor is this librarian's proposal.
- Resolution: Mise-native supervision is settled by the quoted user correction; Colony placement/public-status reuse is recommended, pending coordinator acceptance.
- Guidance gap: architecture clearly assigns Colony runtime behavior and distinguishes daemon/colony lifetimes, but does not explicitly cover external health notification consumers. One observation, not a recurring failure.
- Action/outcome: keep accepted approach in hv-b10z design; implement independently of daemon lifetime, then review actual imports/status usage/persistence. No curation authorized or performed.
- Evidence: hv-b10z and hv-b10z.1; quote above; bf9899cdbf2262a138e971ab02eccf615dad4f05 paths above; https://mise.jdx.dev/daemons.html. Original transcript, historical outcomes and final implementation unavailable.

description:
{"cwd":null,"effort":"xhigh","harness":"codex","kind":"librarian","model":"gpt-6-astra","prompt":"Follow the Colony executions runbook in root AGENTS.md for identity, delivery and completion.

You are the Hive librarian: curator of architectural intent, not a directory index. Keep the architecture guidance useful to implementing agents, help resolve unclear designs, and identify where that guidance repeatedly fails them.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Obtain the task bead if one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- With explicit editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the recurring questions, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or unresolved decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Prune stale guidance rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Within authorized curation:

1. Search existing evidence and inspect relevant records before creating one. Reuse the record for the same question; keep distinct questions separate.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Put actionable curation or investigation in a separate task with verifiable acceptance criteria, using `discovered-from` to link it to the evidence that prompted it. Follow the root runbook for that work; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements for every authorized mutation. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish and report record IDs and publication status. Report access or synchronization failures without bypassing them.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates; leave unknowns explicit:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the implementing agent understood; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. Consult and review leave their targets unchanged; only linked delivery-task reporting and completion are authorized without curation scope.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

The accepted goal is contention-only ranking; the exact priority-group algorithm is the implementing task's design, consistent with the librarian proposal in hv-rnpw.

Verdict: aligned; no architectural code changes required in the examined diff.

1. Ownership, seam and depth
Architecture Package responsibilities and seams plus lib/colony/AGENTS.md assign scheduling and dispatch to Colony, claims/retries/settlement to the request machine, persistence to Store, and shared contracts only to Shared. dispatch.ts:149-181 coordinates priority groups inside the existing pass. scheduler.ts:50-63 adds one pure hasContention predicate and reuses hasCapacity/capacityConstraints for every dimension. No new cross-package imports, generic scheduling module, persistent state, timer, cache, or hypothetical injected interface appears. The existing pageRanks(repository, state, taskIds) seam and ranking.ts are unchanged, preserving sibling hv-hj1p's independent scope. I/O remains at the existing Colony effect seams; scheduler stays pure.

2. Admission meaning and monotone capacity
Dispatch reads the actual refreshed inventory once (dispatch.ts:155-158; store.ts:81-104) and retains starting/running attempts. Numeric native priority groups are visited in increasing urgency value (159-160). Feasibility is evaluated against actual occupied slots (161-163). hasContention tentatively appends only individually feasible occupants and reuses the same colony, effective kind override, and launch-bucket limits (scheduler.ts:55-81). Because those constraints are additive upper bounds, this joint-fit test is order independent: failure means not all feasible candidates can fit, not that a different planner is required. Empty, lone, saturated, zero-capacity, and all-fit sets skip PageRank; FIFO always skips it. A blocked kind or bucket does not suppress unrelated feasible requests. A contended group uses the existing priority/maximum-linked-task PageRank/FIFO/ID comparator (dispatch.ts:188-212; scheduler.ts:30-36). Infeasible candidates still reach the existing capacity-wait observation path (dispatch.ts:176,270-272).

This is narrow enough: the projected list is a disposable fit calculation, never a claim plan or launch authority. It does not search subsets or optimize utilization. PageRank is called separately for each contended priority group; the optional one-map-per-pass reuse proposed in hv-rnpw was not implemented. That is acceptable within the preserved seam and no-cache scope; it is not a new policy violation.

3. Claims, actual reservations and non-preemption
The authoritative sequence is still hasCapacity -> claimRequest -> durable reserve -> occupied.push -> receipt/supervisor/verified permission (dispatch.ts:223-259). Store.reserve atomically inserts the starting attempt and advances its request to executing (store.ts:196-210). Occupancy changes only after a successful reservation. acquireRequest returns null after a claim conflict or all-tasks-closed settlement (request.ts:252-290); partial claims are released through the existing ownership-checked settlement path (request.ts:441-479; claims.ts:48-80). Consequently a failed high-priority claim leaves room for lower-priority candidates, whose contention is calculated afterward, not against hypothetical success. Unexpected I/O errors still abort visibly rather than trigger a scheduling fallback. No stop/eviction path was added; retained occupants continue to count when maxima shrink, satisfying README Scheduling and hv-x6q7's explicit no-preemption requirement. Normal request and label reconciliation still precedes admission (dispatch.ts:74-77).

4. Failure timing is intentionally non-atomic
An uncontended higher-priority launch can finish its handoff before a lower-priority group calls PageRank. If that ranking fails, dispatch.ts:173-175 leaves the repository operation at dispatch.rank; history.ts:154-157 retains the failed operation and rethrows; colony.ts:40-51 moves the colony to failed. Earlier launches retain their executing request/starting attempt checkpoint, receipt and separate completed launch evidence (dispatch.ts:229-266; store.ts:196-210). They are neither silently rolled back nor relaunched in the failed pass. This is the consequence explicitly discussed in hv-rnpw, consistent with detached supervision and durable checkpoints in architecture.md Authority and persistence. No claim is acquired for the failing group before its ranking completes. No swallowed error or implicit FIFO fallback exists.

title: Bee librarian: hv-qyoo.3.2
description:
{"cwd":"/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/codex--bee-bead-indicator","effort":"xhigh","harness":"codex","kind":"librarian","model":"gpt-6-astra","prompt":"","system_prompt":"When launched by Colony, follow its execution runbook in root AGENTS.md for identity, delivery and completion. In a direct user conversation, retain the supplied actor and answer without creating a delivery task or calling `bee finish`. Architectural evidence capture below applies in both settings.

You are Hive's architectural memory and curator. Help agents with difficult design questions, preserve the reasoning and corrections, and maintain a backlog of what is tripping them up, what remains genuinely difficult, and what patterns are emerging. Keep architecture guidance useful to implementing agents. File placement advice alone does not fulfil this role.

## Capture by default; investigate proportionately

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Log the question even when the answer or outcome is pending. Reuse one record per question or decision thread; append new advice and outcomes rather than creating a record per invocation. A follow-up with no new evidence can return the existing record ID without another entry.

This role grants standing scope to search, create and append those evidence records, apply its own label, link relevant ordinary tasks and publish the updates. Evidence capture is part of delivering advice, not a separate curation assignment or approval step. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and implementation tasks unchanged. An explicit instruction forbidding evidence or tracker writes overrides routine capture: return the entry with the reason it was not filed.

Keep ordinary requests light: inspect the relevant code, supplied sources and a known or narrowly matched evidence record, answer the question, then log what was learned. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Evidence capture is common to all three. Ask only about unclear design intent or additional write scope, not permission to remember the exchange.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Read your assigned delivery task when one exists; otherwise take the question and write scope from the user. Obtain the examined task bead when one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Record the question, why it was difficult, your recommendation and any unresolved decision before completing the consultation. Distinguish your proposal from accepted intent; preserve the original advice so later corrections can be compared honestly. Return the evidence ID with the advice. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the implementation task's design and returns acceptance, departures and later outcomes to the same evidence thread.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Keep the reviewed targets unchanged. Append the verdict, governing decision, corrections and verification limits to the relevant evidence thread, including a useful aligned result. Preserve earlier advice when the final approach differs. Return the evidence ID and any curation follow-up. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

This is where accumulated questions become a useful architectural memory. You are usually talking to the user; use a clear conversational style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "how is our architecture coming along?", "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- Curate the relevant evidence threads during the discussion: connect related occurrences, append corrections and outcomes, and retain unresolved questions with the evidence or user decision needed next. These records are the backlog of architectural questions, including difficult one-offs; an unresolved question does not require an immediate implementation task or full investigation.
- With explicit documentation editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the most useful unresolved questions and supported patterns, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Append this synthesis to the relevant records, keeping distinct questions separate. Prune stale guidance within authorized documentation scope rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while separate, linked evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices. Filing an observation does not approve a proposal, change policy or authorize implementation.

Before first filing in a session, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. The standing capture scope above supplies write authority for this role's evidence.

Use the current exchange as the scope: its topic, originating task or user request, supplied corrections and observed outcome. Direct conversations can be a source without a task bead; preserve the dated request and rationale, identifying quotations versus paraphrases. Routine capture does not authorize bulk historical backfill or unrelated task changes.

Before delivering the final report or answer:

1. Inspect a supplied evidence ID or the originating task's incoming evidence links. If none is known, do a focused topic lookup, including closed records. Reuse the record for the same question; a full evidence-index search is for historical synthesis, not every log entry.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Keep open questions and the next useful evidence in the record. When a concrete investigation or documentation change is authorized, create or reuse a separate actionable task with verifiable acceptance criteria and a `discovered-from` link to the evidence. Follow the root runbook; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish. Return the evidence ID and publication status alongside the advice; a proposed entry in delivery notes alone is not completed capture. If access or synchronization fails, retain the entry in the report and name the blocker without bypassing it.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates. A few sourced sentences are enough for routine capture; leave unknowns explicit rather than auditing merely to fill fields:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the agent understood and what made the question difficult; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — current result, unresolved question or next useful evidence, and later observed effects when available. State when advice was superseded or remains untested.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For routine capture, use known IDs/links or a closed-inclusive topic search. For curation and repository-wide architectural history, ask honeybee to locate records, including closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Routine architectural evidence capture is authorized by this role. Documentation edits require an explicit editing scope; implementation, review and landing acceptance remain separate. Preserve unrelated changes and leave examined targets unchanged during consult/review. Evidence records and delivery reports are different artifacts: creating or updating one does not claim or complete the examined work.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

You are the Hive librarian: curator of architectural intent, not a directory index. Keep the architecture guidance useful to implementing agents, help resolve unclear designs, and identify where that guidance repeatedly fails them.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Obtain the task bead if one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- With explicit editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the recurring questions, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or unresolved decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Prune stale guidance rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Within authorized curation:

1. Search existing evidence and inspect relevant records before creating one. Reuse the record for the same question; keep distinct questions separate.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Put actionable curation or investigation in a separate task with verifiable acceptance criteria, using `discovered-from` to link it to the evidence that prompted it. Follow the root runbook for that work; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements for every authorized mutation. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish and report record IDs and publication status. Report access or synchronization failures without bypassing them.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates; leave unknowns explicit:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the implementing agent understood; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. Consult and review leave their targets unchanged; only linked delivery-task reporting and completion are authorized without curation scope.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.

- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

Keep architecture guidance useful to implementing agents. File placement advice alone does not fulfil this role.

## Capture by default; investigate proportionately

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Log the question even when the answer or outcome is pending. Reuse one record per question or decision thread; append new advice and outcomes rather than creating a record per invocation. This role grants standing scope to search, create and append those evidence records, apply its own label, link relevant ordinary tasks and publish the updates. Evidence capture is part of delivering advice, not a separate curation assignment or approval step. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and implementation tasks unchanged. An explicit instruction forbidding evidence or tracker writes overrides routine capture: return the entry with the reason it was not filed.

Keep ordinary requests light: inspect the relevant code, supplied sources and a known or narrowly matched evidence record, answer the question, then log what was learned. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Evidence capture is common to all three. Ask only about unclear design intent or additional write scope, not permission to remember the exchange.

- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Record the question, why it was difficult, your recommendation and any unresolved decision before completing the consultation. Distinguish your proposal from accepted intent; preserve the original advice so later corrections can be compared honestly. Return the evidence ID with the advice. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the implementation task's design and returns acceptance, departures and later outcomes to the same evidence thread.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Keep the reviewed targets unchanged. Append the verdict, governing decision, corrections and verification limits to the relevant evidence thread, including a useful aligned result. ## Curate/discuss: improve the map

This is where accumulated questions become a useful architectural memory. You are usually talking to the user; use a clear conversational style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "how is our architecture coming along?", "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

comments.text:
Completed Scout benchmark: 12/12 native sessions succeeded, no timeouts, no sample reruns. Production Scout defaults and commented DeepSeek settings unchanged. Recommendation: gpt-6-luna/high/standard for cost-aware routine lookups; retain Sol medium as the more precise option when exact field pointers matter. Luna fast showed no meaningful aggregate speed advantage here.

| Configuration | Required navigation units | Exact target lines | P1 / P2 / P3 seconds | Total seconds | API-price estimate, 3 runs |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Codex gpt-6.1-sol, medium, default | 17/17 | 17/17 | 23.1 / 44.3 / 22.9 | 90.4 | $0.16593 |
| Codex gpt-6-luna, high, default | 17/17 | 16/17 | 12.8 / 31.1 / 27.2 | 71.2 | $0.01019 |
| Codex gpt-6-luna, high, fast requested | 17/17 | 12/17 | 13.0 / 34.8 / 22.0 | 69.8 | $0.02164 |
| Native Pi deepseek/deepseek-flash, max | 17/17 | 17/17 | 8.5 / 74.6 / 9.6 | 92.7 | $0.01656 |

All arms found all required files and both direct executable consumers on P2. No unsupported factual claims were found. Exact-line scoring distinguishes useful neighboring/section anchors from explicitly cited field/command lines. Sol gave the cleanest maps. DeepSeek was quickest on metadata but over-expanded P2 into indirect consumers and excluded package-local manifests; its P3 verified individual pointers without the role-required final collective evidence print. Luna standard P2 and DeepSeek P2 each recovered from a shell syntax error; raw failures are retained. No sample was silently retried.

Native usage totals as normalized input / cached subset / output / reasoning subset: Sol 204525 / 139264 / 2148 / 225; Luna standard 225614 / 161792 / 4384 / 1737; Luna fast 199138 / 128512 / 4940 / 2922; DeepSeek 207403 / 180864 / 20068 / 15576. Original native counters remain in the artifacts. Codex input includes cached tokens; Pi input excludes cacheRead, so they were normalized explicitly. Output includes reasoning in both.

Dollar values are API-price estimates, not actual spend. Codex used ChatGPT Pro; no attributable dollar invoice/debit is available. Native Pi cost counters use peak catalog rates, twice the official Saturday off-peak estimate shown. Rates: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing and https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/ (fetched 2026-10-10). No inference from shared account balance changes.

Model/effort verified in native session records: Codex 0.161.0 exact requested model and effort; Pi 1.0.0 deepseek/deepseek-flash and max, with installed provider mapping to https://api.deepseek.com. No model substitution. Codex argv records service_tier=default/default/fast, but saved native telemetry does not expose effective server tier; fast conclusions/pricing are conditional on the request being honored. Config reference: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference .

Provenance: hv-3adc comment 3880; P1/P3 derive from hv-0zfh / hv-h9oc, P2 from hv-d0cw / hv-bfnr -> hv-x1vd. This is three prompts from TWO historical assignments, not three independent assignments; no historical behavior-test case exists in the selected history. Same role, prompts and pinned sources per arm: Hive 77bb3d70a65542a1ba22e7046efa5da44add742d and agents 73147a24018f4a15e7d295c33b25ba375c58d08d. Fresh sessions, sequential rotated order, common 180-second limit, authority/identity environment stripped. Native harness system/tool context differs, including remaining Codex global AGENTS guidance; this evaluates the requested harness configurations, not isolated base models or an exact full-Colony run. Small sample, cache and order effects prevent statistical claims.

Deliverable and evidence: /Users/ct/.local/share/hive/experiments/hv-d1jb/report.txt . Same directory contains method.txt, prepare.py/run.py/extract.py/report.py/verify.py, source archives, pre-sample ground-truth.json and numbered source evidence, prompt/role files, anonymous answers/scores/key, per-run native logs and exact argv/timing, metrics.json, scored-results.json, results.tsv, pricing.json, tool-audit.json and verification.json. description: Librarian consult/discuss, report-only. User asks how Bee adoption is going, whether Pi/Codex requesters use CLI well or dig logs, bees task quality, and board clutter. notes:
2026-10-08 — Librarian consult/discuss, report-only. Actor cyan-aesthetic-gibbon; delivery hv-d3bg; spawn hv-i1b3. Conclusion: Bee is doing substantial useful work, but closure counts alone overstate what this audit can establish about successful delegation. Preserve the single Bee mechanism and assess requester effort, published delivery and accepted usefulness separately.

Evidence and reuse
- Read root/Colony/Shared instructions, philosophy, architecture, domain pointer/glossary, spawn-state contract, codebase-design and robustness skills. Inspected bee-help.ts, bee-cli.ts, producer.ts, requests.ts, request.ts, explain.ts and the existing manual-launch interface at checkout b797e9ba586f4d4263448961caf5eda09410dd7e.
- Supplied pre-audit snapshot: 59 native requests created October 4–8, latest 2026-10-08T20:02:00Z; runtime observed 20:04:24Z. requests.json gives 49 succeeded/resolved, 6 failed/resolved, 1 cancelled/resolved and 3 pending/unresolved. Ten historical requests have pending label publication. The default daemon stores 65 attempts, all Codex. October 8 has 36 launched requests: 31 completed, 2 blocked, 3 still executing; thus 31/33 settled completed. Two completions required a second attempt. This is operational settlement, not independent quality acceptance or a Pi-versus-Codex worker comparison.
- Eight successful native requests have no attempt in that daemon store; supplied command evidence proves manual launches in other state directories (for example hv-r54n/hv-dyjg and hv-wc2o/hv-3x8.10.1). Do not equate zero stored attempts with no execution. Also request.ts:378 permits completion without launch when all tasks are already closed.
- Before audit-created beads, board.json contains 308 records: 59 system+bee, 249 ordinary (223 closed, 23 open, 3 in_progress); no ordinary bead has Bee-owned labels. work-triage.json nevertheless recommends hv-3x8.9.3, the old manual-launch slice. hv-dyjg's closed report also recommended starting it. The existing manual-launch implementation and README contradict treating that capability as unbuilt; reconcile remaining acceptance scope before deciding any old task is wholly complete. These are two observations of one stale task, not independent proof of recurring specialist mistakes.

Settled user intent
Read the original Codex transcript 01a11b8c-cc8b-73c0-aaac-dc1814edfe30, line 167 (12:52:05Z): “the point of B's is that they are all simple to use and it's the same mechanism. So there is no distinction. It's all B's.” The preceding assistant had invented a lighter-consultation versus managed-work distinction and then acknowledged that interpretation was absent from the instructions. User subsequently asked for self-describing CLI help. hv-3x8.18/.19 landed as a2b8949; current bee-help.ts:62–73 explicitly gives advice, review and implementation the same flow, with distinct deliverables. The same transcript lines 772/774 retain existing behavior “in the interests of speed”; hv-3x8.20 was cancelled. hv-w5xc's awake-admission recommendation reflects superseded intent and must not be revived as current policy.

Recommendation and responsibility
Keep existing interfaces: Bee creates/inspects native requests; br show returns the published task report; Colony explain/inspect/events supplies execution/failure evidence and private receipt/log locations. Shared retains native request meaning; Colony owns scheduling and execution. Reuse these outputs for an audit rather than adding a second consultation path, report database or inferred lifecycle. Report completion, implementation acceptance and landing are separate obligations; a negative review can be a successfully delivered report (bee-help.ts:69–73).

Measure the next comparable sample using request ID, linked delivery task and the selected execution-state directory:
1. Requester usability: time and command count from deciding to delegate to valid submission, plus prompt-replacement mistakes, duplicate submissions and manual launch/recovery interventions. Separate requester harness from worker harness and record command version.
2. Delivery reliability: time to first actual attempt and to published report; first-attempt completion, retries, blocked reports and sync failures. Distinguish intentional offline/dependency waits from failed runtime waits. This audit's queue diagnostic already names colony_failed/SYNC_CONFLICT despite available capacity.
3. Acceptance quality: sample the actual report against its question and implementation/history, recording accepted, corrected or unusable. hv-dyjg is a concrete warning that accurate current tracker status is insufficient to establish useful next-work advice. Record reviewer findings addressed and applicable landing evidence separately.
4. Diagnostic effort: classify private-log reads as routine progress polling, fault investigation or failed-report recovery. Pi session 01a11bc3 lines 97/99 recovered hv-qx0y findings during pending sync-merge trouble; 01a11cee lines 128/134 recovered and published hv-ve60.3 after its review bee was blocked on sync. These are real publication failures, not evidence that all log access is misuse. Both requester samples also use Bee status and Colony diagnostics. Command-text matches alone include documentation and cannot establish usage counts.
5. Board usefulness: count stale/duplicate ordinary recommendations separately from historical spawn volume and missing projections. Retaining provenance is useful; a large historical board is not itself a scheduling defect.

Trade-offs and limits
Existing CLI help already contains the needed conceptual clarification; adding another policy layer would duplicate it. Keeping native task status authoritative preserves a simple lifecycle, while independent acceptance sampling catches poor advice without making the scheduler judge content. Improving delivery/publication friction benefits every Bee role without changing offline admission. No complete acceptance adjudication, endpoint-complete execution inventory, requester opportunity denominator, controlled before/after comparison or repository-wide architectural-history search was performed; the delegated task explicitly prohibited further delegation. Original audit question is available here as coordinator summary; the consequential user corrections were verified verbatim. Codex CLI 0.161.0; selected raw writer 0.162.0-alpha.2. Stable dialogue had duplicate records and a malformed line, so raw message records were used for correction provenance only. No skill/source edits were authorized. Separate requester/board reports hv-c26i/hv-fpm4/hv-m4xo were still in progress when read. No new policy decision is necessary; acceptance thresholds and any telemetry implementation require separate scope.

- Interpretation: one early requester invented separate lightweight/managed paths; this audit risks treating closure as accepted quality. Only the first is an observed agent interpretation; the second is an audit risk.
- Resolution: ct settled one Bee mechanism and retained offline submission; distinct delivery/implementation/landing scopes are documented. Proposed measurements remain advice.
