title: Consult on Colony event subscriptions and subscriber hosting
description:
Mode: consult only, for an ongoing live design discussion. Keep the report focused; do not delegate further or search architectural history. Inspect current canonical code read-only; no implementation, curation, policy decisions, commits, or application writes are authorized. Only deliver and complete this report task through the normal Colony runbook.

Original user request: create an inbuilt event system in each colony so code can listen and act, moving hard-coded automations such as post-run assessment into repository configuration. User now asks to discuss a blessed TypeScript module loaded in Colony versus an event stream any service can consume. Their rationale: in-process integration seems easier but multiple colonies in one daemon complicate module separation; an event socket decouples consumers but somebody must start them.

Current findings: lib/colony/src/request.ts settlement directly calls prepareAssessment from postrun.ts; store.ts atomically saves enrollment with terminal checkpoint; dispatch.ts calls reconcileAssessments; postrun.ts owns assessment-specific prompt, report schema, serial queue, five-minute deadline. drone.ts separately handles inactivity inspection with consequences for retries. Config already chooses drone kinds. Nurse is manually invoked. colony events/history.ts is bounded diagnostic operation history, not a durable subscriber contract. Architecture says one daemon hosts multiple per-repository colonies; private SQLite and scheduling remain in Colony. Relevant docs: docs/architecture.md, GLOSSARY.md, lib/colony/README.md.

Explore the simplest useful seam, especially process isolation versus event contract, per-repository/tracker scoping, who starts a managed subscriber, and whether one-shot handler processes could avoid a permanently running service. Preserve distinctions between execution attempts, settled requests and advisory assessments. Assess provisional idea: a durable request.settled event with a repository-configured handler; Colony can own delivery and start a separate handler process without knowing assessment semantics. Do not design a general broker or recommend libraries; this is a conceptual discussion. State durability/replay requirements proportionately and avoid exactly-once claims. Return tradeoffs and at most two material unanswered user choices.
acceptance_criteria: Record concise evidence-grounded advice comparing in-process TypeScript handlers, externally managed socket subscribers, and Colony-managed subscriber processes; distinguish proposals from current behavior and identify user decisions. No code, configuration, or architecture-document edits.
notes:
Additional live user question: How would someone subscribe? Is there one daemon socket or sockets per colony? They explicitly distinguish the Colony daemon from each individual colony and want terminology clarified. Include a concrete proposed subscription addressed by canonical repository and selected tracker, distinguishing current control transport from a proposed event stream. Please keep advice concise for this live conversation.
Consult report — 2026-10-09 — canonical revision 908ac2a963381625969fdf5d15922a56a68ccc43

Evidence and reuse
Read-only inspection of the clean supplied checkout; user intent is taken from this task's description and live-question note, not an independently inspected conversation transcript. No historical search or delegation.
- One daemon hosts repository colonies through one Unix control socket (server.ts:53,80,290; client.ts:33). A colony is the repository's scheduling/reconciliation activity, not a daemon process. The registry keys by canonical root and rejects a different tracker for that root (server.ts:354); this is not simultaneous multi-tracker hosting.
- request.ts:481 directly prepares assessments; store.ts:161 saves enrollment with the request checkpoint in one SQLite transaction. dispatch.ts:59 reconciles them. postrun.ts:159,213,315 owns eligibility, serial execution, prompts and reporting. The existing process ownership/supervision mechanisms are useful reuse, although their harness-shaped launch receipts need adaptation for arbitrary handlers.
- README.md:244-248 describes advisory assessment semantics: one per launched settled request across attempts, no historical backfill, one launch/five minutes, no automatic retry. Inactivity reviews affect live-attempt retry decisions and remain a distinct responsibility (request.ts:410; README.md:230-238).
- colony events is bounded offline diagnostic history, not an event feed or delivery queue (history.ts:11; README.md:364-375). The separately supervised watchdog is an existing external-consumer example, currently polling control status (bin/watchdog.ts:44; README.md:307-346).
Paths above are under lib/colony; governing guidance is docs/architecture.md and GLOSSARY.md.

Recommendation — proposal, not accepted policy
Separate the event contract from how consumers run. Start with a durable request.settled fact and a repository-configured, Colony-managed one-shot handler. For example, canonical .hive/bees.toml could name an event, stable handler ID and argv launching Bun with a proposed new .hive/handlers/post-run.ts. Colony starts it with an immutable scoped event on stdin; successful exit acknowledges processing, failure remains visible. A TS module can therefore be the authoring interface without being imported into the shared daemon.

Colony owns event persistence, scoped delivery and process lifecycle; the handler owns assessment meaning, prompt, evidence assembly and report format. Keep the scheduler/private database in Colony. Handlers consume event data and supported scoped inspection interfaces, not internal store imports. Adapt the existing settlement transaction and process ownership code; neither repurposing diagnostic history nor launching an ordinary task request preserves the desired semantics. Put event delivery in a proposed Colony-local module such as lib/colony/src/events.ts; only place a wire contract in Shared when actual cross-package consumers need it.

How to subscribe — proposed, not available today
Use the selected daemon's existing socket, with a new streaming endpoint, rather than one socket per colony. An illustrative subscription on that endpoint:
{"kind":"subscribe","repository":{"root":"/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive","beadsDb":"/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/tracker--state/.beads/beads.db"},"topics":["request.settled"],"after":"<saved cursor>"}
Carry the same repository/tracker pair on every event, alongside stable event ID, request ID, terminal outcome and attempt references. Validate the tracker against the registered root. A stream must sit outside server.ts's serialized control-command queue; an open subscription must not block sleep/wake commands. A cursor resumes reading, not proof that effects completed. For managed one-shot handlers, config is the subscription and no permanently connected client is required. Externally managed consumers would maintain their own processing checkpoint.

Trade-offs
- In-process TS: least launch overhead and convenient functions; requires explicit per-colony instances/disposal and scoped dependencies. Module globals, CPU work or process failure can affect every colony. Per-repository imports alone do not isolate them.
- External socket consumer: independent language, deployment and lifetime; the user/service manager must start, restart and reconnect it. A socket does not solve hosting. This remains useful for already-running services and daemon-health observers.
- Colony-managed process: isolates handler memory/process failures and removes separate service setup. Colony gains delivery/ownership bookkeeping and process startup cost. One-shot work is sufficient for assessments; a resident managed subscriber adds reconnect/readiness lifecycle without a demonstrated need. Process separation under the same OS user is not a security sandbox.

Durability and meaning
Record the event with the terminal checkpoint after existing native settlement publication; retain replayable pending deliveries and per-handler outcomes. This local transaction does not make Beads and SQLite one atomic store. Restart recovery may redeliver after effects happened but acknowledgment was lost: use stable event/handler identities and idempotent effects, never exactly-once claims. Propose visible failed delivery plus explicit retry initially, not an invented automatic retry policy or unlimited event archive.
request.settled means the request reached its final outcome, not one attempt exited or tasks necessarily succeeded. Settlement alone is not evidence of stopped processes. Preserve the current assessment's stopped-process gate and launched-request eligibility in the configured behavior. Handler failure must not reopen/retry the original request; auxiliary handler completion must not recursively become another ordinary request settlement. Inactivity verdict authority should not be replaced by an advisory subscriber as part of this seam.

Two material choices
1. Is Colony-managed one-shot execution the default authoring experience, or must the first version support independently hosted live subscribers?
2. Is restart-safe processing of events enrolled while a subscription is configured enough, or must newly added/reconnected consumers replay earlier history? Proposed minimum: preserve enrolled work; no retroactive backfill. Managed delivery follows the colony's existing awake/asleep reconciliation policy.

Proposed architectural-friction entry (not filed)
- architectural-friction — 2026-10-09; colony-event-subscriber-hosting; event contract versus subscriber hosting.
- Interpretation — task records the user's distinction between daemon and individual colonies, and concern that a socket leaves subscriber startup unsolved; managed one-shot delivery is librarian advice.
- Resolution — pending user choice; no policy approved.
- Guidance gap — missing extension contract; current ownership guidance is clear but does not define subscriptions.
- Action/outcome — proposal only; a later design should demonstrate scoped delivery to two repositories, restart recovery, and handler failure independent of request outcome.
- Evidence — hv-l58p description/live-question note; revision 908ac2a; paths above. One observation, not a recurring trend.

Verification: inspected current implementation and governing docs; no code/configuration/documentation edits, tests, commits or application writes. Quality suites were unnecessary for this read-only consultation. Only this report task is being updated and completed.
User has now authorized implementation of an efficient events API anyone can consume, initially TypeScript, with schemas exported as a consumable library. Accepted direction: one socket per daemon, events carry colony identity, filtering can select multiple colonies for one consumer. Implementation task will be separate; this remains consult only. Please prioritize placement of exported event schemas/client: Shared is current contract owner, product cross-imports prohibited, all packages currently private. Considering @hive/shared/colony-events as focused public subpath. Recommend smallest event stream interface with efficient live notification and durable replay; no configurable handler host needed in first API slice. User is being asked whether assessment migration should happen now or after API/example, and whether registry release is intended.
Consult addendum — 2026-10-09 — supersedes the first report's managed-handler-first recommendation

Accepted direction, as recorded in the new coordinating-agent note: one daemon socket; events identify their colony; one consumer can select multiple colonies; consumable TypeScript schemas/client. Implementation is a separate task. No handler hosting is required in this first slice.

Placement and smallest interface
Recommend @hive/shared/colony-events for runtime schemas and inferred types, with a focused @hive/shared/colony-events/client subpath for the stream client. Proposed files: lib/shared/src/colony-events.ts and colony-events-client.ts, exported explicitly by lib/shared/package.json. Reuse RepositoryEndpoint's root/beadsDb meaning. This matches lib/shared/AGENTS.md and docs/architecture.md: contracts shared by producer and consumers live in Shared; daemon persistence, filtering and stream serving stay in Colony. The client must import no Colony internals, start no daemon, and perform no repository discovery. Keep it separate from Colony's control client, whose fixed request timeout/one-document response do not suit streams.

An illustrative TypeScript interface (proposal, not existing code):
subscribeColonyEvents({ socket, state, colonies: [{ root, beadsDb }, ...], topics: ["request.settled"], after, signal }): AsyncIterable<ColonyEvent>
Each colony selector is an exact repository/tracker pair, not separate root and tracker lists whose cross-product might select unintended endpoints. A single stream merges matching events in durable log order. This does not add support for registering multiple trackers for the same canonical root in one daemon.

One proposed POST /events endpoint on the selected daemon socket accepts that subscription and streams newline-delimited JSON. Keep POST / control requests and this stream distinct; stream setup/lifetime must not occupy server.ts's serialized lifecycle-command promise. A public framing/schema contract lets other languages consume it later. The initial client may explicitly target Bun, matching the repository runtime; TypeScript types alone do not establish Node/browser Unix-socket compatibility.

Efficient live notification and durable replay
- A Colony-owned event module (proposed lib/colony/src/events.ts, composed by store.ts/server.ts) appends immutable events with the terminal checkpoint in the existing SQLite transaction, then notifies live readers after commit. It owns indexed, paged reads and wakeups. Events include a stable ID/cursor, type, canonical root/tracker, timestamp, request ID, outcome and relevant attempt references.
- Use a monotonic log sequence scoped to a persistent log identity, not a daemon-process identity. An opaque cursor survives restart but cannot silently address a different/recreated store. Sequence gaps after filtering are valid.
- A subscriber reads committed rows after its cursor in bounded pages, drains through the current tail, then awaits commit notification. Register the wakeup before the final tail check, or use an equivalent generation check, so replay-to-live has no missed-event window. Wakeups mean “read new rows”; persisted rows remain the source. Avoid per-consumer interval polling or unbounded in-memory event queues.
- Apply stream backpressure; a slow/disconnected reader resumes from its saved cursor. The consumer records its cursor only after processing. A crash can repeat an effect; no exactly-once guarantee. No durable server-side consumer registry or acknowledgments are needed in the first stream API.
- Define a bounded retention window and explicit cursor-expired/wrong-log failure; never silently jump to the live tail. Make a fresh subscription's start position explicit (live now versus retained history). Old diagnostic operations are not backfilled into domain events.

A request.settled event still means final request outcome, not individual attempt exit or guaranteed process termination. Existing post-run assessments and inactivity policy stay in place unless their migration is explicitly chosen. API/example first avoids adding both subscriber hosting and assessment ownership changes to the transport slice; that ordering is a proposal.

Publication and remaining user choices
lib/shared/package.json currently has private: true, version 0.0.0 and only the root export; all product packages are private. Adding a subpath makes it consumable inside the workspace/local package but does not make it registry-installable. A registry release would require an explicitly scoped packaging decision; the repository currently runs TypeScript source directly with no build/emit. Do not silently promise arbitrary Node/browser consumption or publish Shared.
The two questions already being taken to the user are sufficient: (1) migrate assessments now or after the event API/example, and (2) local/workspace consumption or registry release? The earlier hosting question has been superseded by the accepted stream-first direction.

Proposed architectural-friction update (not filed)
Topic colony-event-subscriber-hosting: the coordinating note now records a user decision for a multiplexed daemon stream and exported schemas. Recommended host contract:
1. Shared owns a request-level host field in the existing spawn description, decoded separately from Recipe; do not add routing to kind defaults or formula rendering. Small interface: readSpawnRequest returns host (string or explicit unbound null) with identity/recipe/taskIds. Colony captures OS hostname automatically at submission and owns local-host comparisons. No caller flag, inferred cwd/actor host, GUID registry or current-host default for old records.
2. Admit local bound requests before any automatic lifecycle effect: dispatch discovery before publishRequestLabels/newRequest; reconcileRequests for saved checkpoints before claiming-state transitions, process recovery, observations, claim release and settlement; reconcileClosedRequestLabels; manual prepareLaunch before filesystem/receipt/process effects. A single launch check is insufficient because dispatch reconciles and repairs labels first.
3. Retain host with captured identity/taskIds in durable request authority and validate it on reconciliation/retry. Do not silently adopt old unbound checkpoints. Automatic attempts keep the request's host. Explicit bee retry creates a replacement on the caller's host, per hv-lqeh.1.
4. Check every target of automatic label publication, including supersedes predecessors: a local replacement does not authorize its Colony to repair a foreign/unbound predecessor. Pass explicit automatic-host authority through that existing operation; do not infer authority from actor text. Explicit offline stop/ack/retry are separate user-initiated operations and can retain their existing native publication contract.
5. Keep unbound history inspectable and visibly unbound. Queued unbound requests require deliberate stop/recreation on the intended host; existing live unbound attempts require a deliberate drain/upgrade decision, not hostname backfill. No migration or live repair is authorized by this consult. Hostname equality assumes unique, stable hostnames; it is routing, not distributed exclusivity for different requests against the same task.

Recommended merge contract and concrete concern:
- Keep the existing mergeIssueJsonl seam. Treat integer comment IDs as transport-local. Merge append-only identities (issue_id, author, text, created_at) with maximum per-side multiplicity, then render deterministic globally unique local IDs. Compare the remaining scalar record using conservative three-way selection, ignoring derived updated_at only. Never choose claims or closure by the newer timestamp. Keep genuine scalar and issue delete/edit conflicts visible.
- FIX/ASSESS BEFORE LANDING: Shared latestColonyObservation and latestStdoutActivity currently choose max local comment ID. A focused in-memory probe against the WIP merge core produced a newer settled comment at 00:00:02 with rekeyed id 1 while older running at 00:00:01 retained id 11; the current reader selected running. lib/colony/src/observations.ts also uses those readers for deduplication. Use immutable timestamps for reader ordering (stdout recordedAt and native observation created_at), with documented deterministic ties independent of ID. Same-second native comments lack enough evidence for exact causal order; do not pretend a tie-breaker reconstructs it. Avoid coupling the merge driver to Colony event text.
- This design trades automatic resolution of independent scalar edits for a small conservative driver. It does not heal already divergent closures, serialize cross-clone writers, or distinguish independent byte-identical same-timestamp comments beyond observed multiplicity. Those limits are preferable to silently selecting ownership.

## Standards sources

## Brief

Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces (oxlint and oxfmt already pass on this revision).

## Smell baseline (Fowler, Refactoring ch.3)

- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

Current assessment module depends on runtime.store for target RequestRecord/LaunchReceipt, queue/report checkpoints and report authority; worker supervision depends on receipt/env; dispatch reconciles assessment queue; bee assess reads private store. How much should move to make this real dogfooding without writing a general process host? Compare a daemon-hosted automation module consuming the actual socket/SDK with a separate command/process and its own assessment store. Favor smallest coherent module; identify what event/public inspection data a genuine external assessor requires. Current candidate settlement event includes request ID/identity/outcome/task IDs plus attempt ID, kind, harness/model/cwd and evidence-directory references, never tokens/prompts. A module may use retained source files as evidence but must not import request/scheduler state to infer settlement. Preserve advisory authority, per-repository serial assessment, stopped-process gate, no recursion, one launch/five-minute deadline, explicit missing coverage, disabling new enrollment without abandoning current inspection. Consult report — 2026-10-09 — hv-m1ts.1
Examined baseline 908ac2a963381625969fdf5d15922a56a68ccc43 in feat--colony-event-api. Existing event-library work in the shared worktree belongs to the implementing agent and was left untouched. Read hv-m1ts.1, hv-m1ts and the supplied prior report hv-l58p; no delegation or history search. User intent is available through their recorded words/rationale in those tasks, not an independently examined conversation transcript.

Evidence and reuse
- The accepted correction is real assessment dogfooding now, because an API plus example may not serve automation. This supersedes hv-l58p's API/example-first advice. One daemon socket, scoped replay and focused Shared schemas/client are settled direction; hosting and extraction below are proposals.
- request.ts:442–481 prepares assessment source before committing settlement; store.ts:161 atomically saves enrollment and the terminal checkpoint; dispatch.ts:59 reconciles the queue. postrun.ts:159,213,315 owns eligibility, all-attempt evidence, serial execution and report authority. Paths here are under lib/colony/src.
- inspection.ts:10 and Shared colony-protocol.ts expose safe attempt metadata and paths, but retained states are historical, not stopped-process proof. postrun.ts:231 currently checks every target receipt through processes.ts:127 before launch. request.ts:390 also stops the current attempt during settlement.
- postrun.ts:315 currently spreads a target LaunchReceipt to create the assessor's receipt. This is convenience coupling, not required target authority. launch.ts:207 and bin/worker.ts already support detached assessment execution, injected authority and deadline; reuse them for the assessor's OWN execution.
- README.md:244–264 and docs/architecture.md require advisory authority, no backfill/zero-launch inspection, one inspector per repository, one launch/five minutes, explicit missing coverage and offline retrieval. postrun.smoke.test.ts:181–221,299–340,418–439 documents recovery, disabling, seriality and interrupted-reservation behavior. These tests were read, not run.

Recommendation — smallest coherent extraction
Keep an assessment automation module inside lib/colony, hosted by server.ts alongside colony actors. Proposed new postrun-consumer.ts owns the public subscription and lifecycle; proposed postrun-store.ts owns assessment persistence. Adapt existing postrun.ts, postrun-evidence.ts and assessments.ts rather than creating a product package or general handler host. The consumer must actually connect to the daemon socket through @hive/shared/colony-events/client. An in-memory callback carrying the same event type would not satisfy this dogfooding.

Remove prepareAssessment from request settlement and reconcileAssessments from dispatch. Replace Store.settleRequest's assessment parameter with atomic terminal-checkpoint + immutable request.settled append. No assessment configuration, prompt construction or task snapshot reads remain on that settlement path. Inactivity drone decisions stay in Colony's request lifecycle.

The host supplies explicit repository/tracker, socket, consumer-state location, effective assessment configuration/revision and lifecycle cancellation. It does not supply RequestRecord, daemon Store or target LaunchReceipt. A small start/configure/pause/close interface is sufficient. Shared owns the public event/inspection contracts and consumer transport, never assessment scheduling or persistence. Reusing Colony-local supervision for the consumer's own inspector does not invalidate public-input dogfooding; it does mean this slice is not a separately deployable assessor package.

Persistence and delivery
Use consumer-owned assessments.sqlite under the selected state directory, with its own cursor/inbox, enrollment identity, jobs and report authority. This avoids a new dependency on daemon tables and lets bee assess and colony assessments keep their offline behavior through postrun-store.ts. Keep separate report authority/deadline checks; relocate readAssessmentAuthority out of store.ts. Construct each inspector receipt from its own configuration, identity, directory and token, not by cloning a target receipt.

For each event, atomically insert the input/job (or record an intentional skip) and advance the consumer cursor. Persist before evidence reads or launch; cursor acknowledgment means durable intake, not report completion. Key deduplication by log identity + exact repository/tracker + request/settlement identity. A crash after intake cannot lose the job; replay cannot create another launch. Preserve reserved/reviewing/decided/finished checkpoints and the existing no-retry rule. The producer event transaction and consumer intake transaction are separate; do not promise exactly-once effects.

Fresh installation establishes and saves a public live-tail baseline before dispatch starts; no old terminal-request scan. Restart uses its saved cursor and jobs. A wrong-log/expired cursor becomes visible missing coverage requiring explicit recovery, never a silent jump to tail. Public checkpoint/watermark frames must advance filtered consumers even when no matching settlement arrives. Retention remains a stated coverage bound, not a guarantee of unlimited offline recovery.

Public data needed
The candidate event needs ALL attempt references, not only the final attempt: request ID, captured identity/task IDs, terminal outcome, settlement timestamp, repository/tracker, log cursor, and safe attempt IDs/numbers/kind/harness/model/cwd/evidence references. Include reliable launch evidence so reservations are not mistaken for launched work. Prompts, invocation arguments and execution tokens stay out of the event.

Add a focused public request inspection operation, adapting inspection.ts and exporting its schema/client through Shared. It must support:
1. Fresh, timestamped ownership-verified stopped/live observation for every target attempt. The server performs observeExecution with private authority; unknown or unverifiable ownership fails visibly and never passes the launch gate. Current retained attempt.state is insufficient. The consumer does not import process ownership or receipt schemas to interpret target state.
2. Explicitly requested captured-source evidence (role/prompt) or a documented, typed local source manifest, plus attempt/log locations. Reuse safe existing projections. Raw target LaunchReceipt is not the public contract. A same-machine assessor may read retained logs and exact thread-linked rollouts for evidence; files do not establish settlement.
3. Explicit unavailable evidence reasons. Native task snapshots can use Shared's Beads interface with the event's exact tracker/task IDs; absent logs, tasks or telemetry remain uncertainty, not fabricated empty evidence.

Keep the stopped-target check distinct from supervision of the inspector itself. An external assessor supplies its own launch configuration and process management; it does not need a generic launch endpoint or the inspected worker's token.

Configuration, sleep and recovery
Persist the consumer's configured policy epochs before enabling each producer epoch. Put the effective SETTLEMENT policy revision ID on events (not merely the attempt's launch revision); the host records that revision's enabled/disabled assessment configuration in the consumer store. Replay then uses policy in force at settlement, rather than today's toggle. This preserves no enrollment for disabled periods even if consumption lagged across reset/restart. Inspector invocation remains captured at launch as today; queued jobs wait while disabled, already-started jobs still reconcile.

Start socket serving before awaiting any self-subscription. Stream handling and necessary read-only inspection must not wait behind a lifecycle command that is itself draining the consumer: server.ts:80 currently serializes control commands, so careless self-calls can deadlock.

Sleep/remove first drain the producer pass, then stop consumer launch/reconciliation and finish in-flight durable intake. Undelivered events remain replayable; pending intake must retain its old policy epoch. Detached inspectors continue, enforcing their five-minute deadline, and may publish reports while asleep. On wake, restore consumer state and reconcile active work before another queued launch; on daemon stop abort streams/await local loops before closing stores, without killing detached workers. Recovery of durable awake registrations reloads canonical policy and restores recorded jobs/cursor; a sleeping registration waits for wake. Assessment failure never reopens, retries, claims or changes the target request. Auxiliary inspector execution creates no ordinary spawn/settlement event, preventing recursion. Persist/show consumer infrastructure failures separately; do not turn them into target-request failures or silently discard the consumer.

Trade-offs and unresolved decision
Daemon hosting is the smaller step: it already owns repository membership, config activation and sleep, while the expensive assessor remains a detached process. Its cost is shared daemon failure/CPU fate and careful async shutdown. A separate command with its own assessment store would prove deployment independence, but adds who-starts/restarts-it, single-owner enforcement, live policy/sleep observation and packaging of execution support. A socket alone solves none of these. Defer that host until demanded; this extraction must already make settlement/evidence inputs public.

One semantic decision remains: task snapshots currently read during settlement will instead be read at consumer intake/preparation. Recommend recording observedAt and documenting that timing honestly. Replay may see later task edits; neither a timestamp nor an inspection endpoint reconstructs settlement-time text. If exact settlement-time task content must be retained, keep a GENERIC immutable task-evidence snapshot with the producer's settlement evidence and expose its reference publicly, accepting the additional producer IO. The coordinating agent should resolve/document this departure rather than silently claiming unchanged snapshots. Registry release remains outside scope.

Verification target for implementation: a real socket/SDK test should replay a settlement after daemon restart, enroll once into the independent store, inspect all target attempts, run one advisor, retrieve its report offline, and preserve sleep/disable/deadline behavior without request/dispatch calls into assessment code. Include lag across policy changes and missing-source coverage. This report supplies design, not a passing implementation review.

Consult report — 2026-10-09 — hv-m1ts.3

Recommendation: retain request.settled as the first useful contract. The smallest next set is request.retry_scheduled and colony.activity_changed, driven by retry visibility and failure/sleep alerts. Add attempt lifecycle events when an execution timeline is the next concrete consumer. Keep assessment, nurse, scheduling and listener-delivery facts with their respective external owners. The catalogue below is a prioritized set of proposals, not authorization to implement every event.

Evidence and reuse

Read this task's full description and four acceptance criteria, hv-m1ts, hv-m1ts.2, and the supplied consultations hv-l58p and hv-m1ts.1. Examined HEAD 908ac2a963381625969fdf5d15922a56a68ccc43 plus the actively edited, uncommitted event/listener spike in feat--colony-event-api. File references below refer to that observed working tree; implementation is continuing concurrently. Read root/package instructions, PHILOSOPHY, architecture, domain guidance, GLOSSARY and codebase-design/robustness skills. No wider history search or delegation.

The task quotes the user: “Bear in mind, from memory, the existing sort of nurse bee relationship puts data in the colony. That was expedient for the agents building it out, but we'd probably refactor that completely, so colony no longer owns that.” This is supplied original wording; I have not independently inspected the originating conversation. It supersedes the earlier librarian proposal for daemon-hosted assessment consumption. The eventual external owner is settled direction for this discussion; its package name, persistence, hosting and migration behavior are not decided.

Current implementation versus proposals:
- The spike's lib/shared/src/colony-events.ts exposes ONLY request.settled. lib/colony/src/store.ts:164–191 appends it with the terminal request checkpoint (and existing assessment enrollment) in one SQLite transaction, then notifies readers.
- lib/colony/src/events.ts provides a separate durable journal, exact repository/tracker filtering, persistent log identity/cursors and bounded replay over POST /events on the daemon socket. server.ts:85–90 routes streaming outside the serialized control-command queue. No second per-colony socket is needed.
- The existing .hive/listeners/settlement-log and assessment-intake examples consume the public typed listener. assessment-intake currently records evidence availability; it is not a migrated assessor. Existing assessment orchestration still runs through request.ts:481, dispatch.ts:59 and postrun.ts.
- Existing colony events/history.ts is bounded operation diagnostics, including partial effects and failures. Its start-sequence and mutable operation records are not the public domain journal.
- docs/architecture.md and lib/colony/README.md describe the presently implemented assessment coupling. They are not evidence that the user approved keeping it. No documentation changes are authorized here.

Common contract

Reuse the spike envelope: {cursor:{logId,sequence}, type, repository:{root,beadsDb}, recordedAt}. The pair identifies a colony; an ID alone is not globally scoped. Cursor order is this daemon journal's commit order, not global causality, wall-clock ordering or a process-start timestamp. Existing registration permits one tracker per canonical root in a daemon; selecting multiple pairs does not change that rule.

Fields below are the event-specific minimum in addition to that envelope. recordedAt means Colony recorded the fact. Add an explicit source/observation timestamp only when the source actually supplies one; never relabel reconciliation time as execution time. Reference logs/evidence through supported inspection, not broad prompt, token, invocation, transcript or log payloads. Runtime schemas/types/client stay in Shared's focused event exports; persistence, transition decisions and emission stay in Colony. No consumer imports Colony's private Store or LaunchReceipt to infer lifecycle truth.

Responsibility and semantic limits

1. Request outcome and resolution have different lifetimes. request.settled currently carries Colony terminal outcomes completed/cancelled/exhausted/claim_failed/blocked (Shared spawn-request.ts:48), not query dispositions pending/succeeded/failed/cancelled. Completed can mean all linked tasks were already closed without a launch. Failed outcomes do not imply unresolved forever: later acknowledgment or supersession resolves follow-up without rewriting the failure. Avoid a second request.failed or request.completed event duplicating a filter over request.settled.

2. request.settled covers Colony-managed checkpoints, not every native spawn closure. A request created and stopped offline before any awake pass may never have a checkpoint/event. Native Beads remains request/task authority. request.ts performs verified cleanup of the current attempt, but a historical settlement event is not fresh proof that every referenced process tree is stopped; postrun.ts:213–240 deliberately checks ALL source attempts separately.

3. Command success is specific. spawn_created confirms native request creation, not launch. request_stopped records native closure, not stopped execution. finish_submitted confirms an immutable finish artifact; Colony still checks current-attempt authority and task state, and success with unfinished work may retry. blocked is terminal unsuccessful handoff, not ordinary waiting. drone_verdict_submitted is not an accepted decision. Wake installs scheduling but does not prove a healthy completed pass; sleep acknowledges drain while detached workers continue. No generic command.accepted event should be treated as any of these effects.

4. Reuse the current journal, not history.run diagnostics or XState input event names. INTEND/SETTLE/STOP are commands/internal transitions; tracker.show, receipt.write and supervisor.spawned are diagnostic effects. A public event needs an independently useful domain meaning. Keep errors' operation detail in bounded diagnostics; expose colony failure or final request outcome as the relevant public fact.

5. Add each new event at its authoritative durable commit, then notify. The current journal has UNIQUE(root,beads_db,type,request_id), which fits one settlement per request but cannot support repeated retry/output/claim events or colony-only events. Event-specific durable occurrence identity is required when expanding it: attempt ID for attempt milestones, review ID for decisions, revision ID for policy, prior attempt for retry, and a persisted transition identity for repeated observations. Do not merely add enum members and silently drop repeat occurrences. This is an extension constraint, not a defect in the one-event spike.

6. Do not append lifecycle events from store.inventory's read/refresh path merely because it is convenient: status calls also use it. Explicit reconciliation owns execution observations. Recovery must deduplicate already recorded facts; an observation stream should state if intermediate offline transitions can be absent. A read model plus changes also needs a defined snapshot/cursor handoff before claiming full dashboard reconstruction.

These have their own scope/lifetime. watchdog.ts already owns outage observation/checkpoints. | Scheduled nurse work, restart/operator alerts. No Colony tick/cron event is needed. A dead daemon cannot reliably publish its own unavailability; disconnect alone is not proof of a colony failure or stopped workers. |

Assessment/nurse extraction implications

The external assessor should own enrollment, configuration, inbox/checkpoint, deduplication, launch/report lifecycle, evidence interpretation, reports and missing-coverage records; the nurse owns synthesis. A canonical .hive/listeners definition is authoring/discovery, not daemon ownership of its process. External startup is explicit in this spike. Keep inactivity review authority in Colony because its decisions affect current attempt cleanup/retry.

The useful Colony contract is settled request + safe evidence access. The spike has all reserved attempt IDs and receipt paths, while inspection.ts and Shared colony-protocol.ts:108–143 already project safe metadata/log paths. Reuse those projections. A receipt path alone should not force consumers to deserialize private tokens/prompts or infer sibling-file layout. Real assessment extraction still needs supported captured-source access and fresh ownership-verified stopped observations, including explicit unavailable evidence. Put sensitive requested source behind a focused evidence interface rather than broad events. Which endpoint/artifact contract supplies it remains open.

Do not add assessment.ready to Colony merely to make that first consumer convenient. Likewise, a listener can perform bee/br effects, but automatic retry, killing an execution, task acceptance and workflow progression retain their existing authorities. Delivery may replay after effects but before checkpoint save; cursor acknowledgment is consumer progress, not exactly-once effects. External side effects need consumer-owned deduplication/intake. Higher-volume event families also compete with the current bounded journal retention; do not promise a time window based solely on a count cap.

Trade-offs and unresolved decisions

The proposed first additions give alerts and retry visibility using meaningful state changes without turning private scheduler choreography into a public protocol. Keeping attempt/claim/output detail later avoids committing to incomplete process histories or high-volume data before a consumer requires it. Per-event contracts have clearer meaning than publishing every private request state or raw operation log; their cost is explicit emission/deduplication work at each owner.

Decisions to resolve when selecting the next slice:
- Is the next consumer retry/failure alerts, a complete execution timeline, or full assessment extraction? Recommend alerts after validating the current settlement spike; these call for different data guarantees.
- Does the public feed intentionally cover only daemon-managed observations, or must it include native requests/tasks changed while offline, including pre-observation closure and later acknowledgment/supersession? The latter needs a native-fact ingestion design, not stronger wording on settlement.
- Must attempt starts/ends be exhaustive, or is documented observation coverage enough? Exhaustive lifecycle milestones need durable source evidence, not polling of a replaced worker snapshot.
- For the external assessor, who starts it, what policy determines enrollment during replay/disabled periods, does colony sleep pause it, and when are task contents captured? Prior daemon-hosted/policy-epoch recommendations are proposals superseded in hosting scope, not settled external policy. “Current task text when consumed” and “text at settlement” are different guarantees. Also decide the supported public evidence/stopped-process interface.
No new policy, packaging release, scheduler, external storage location or migration behavior is decided by this report.

Proposed architectural-friction entry — not filed

- architectural-friction — 2026-10-09; colony-event-fact-ownership; which public facts Colony owns versus native Beads and external assessment/nurse modules.
- Interpretation — prior implementation placed advisory state in Colony; earlier librarian advice retained daemon hosting. The current task supplies the user's correction that this was expedient and should be refactored out.
- Resolution — external assessment/nurse ownership and independent listener execution are current direction. Event names, external storage/hosting, native-fact coverage and evidence access above remain proposals or open decisions.
- Guidance gap — missing public event/evidence ownership contract; current documentation explains implemented coupling but does not yet encode the prospective separation.
- Action/outcome — catalogue only; no evidence record or documentation writes. A later consultation/review can verify that a real assessor consumes public settled/evidence contracts, owns its persistence, and does not import the daemon Store, while offline native changes are not mislabeled as immediate Colony effects.
- Evidence — hv-m1ts.3 original quoted correction and scope; hv-m1ts/hv-m1ts.2; earlier hv-l58p and hv-m1ts.1 advice; baseline 908ac2a plus uncommitted spike paths above. This is one decision thread, not evidence of a recurring trend or validated improvement.

Read-only consult completed. No code, configuration, architecture documents, unrelated tasks, labels, evidence records or application Git history changed by this report. Existing concurrent spike edits were left untouched. No tests/quality suites were run: this is a catalogue consultation, not final-diff approval, and the spike is actively changing. The startup tracker publication succeeded with its normal hooks. Only hv-m1ts.3 is being recorded/completed; final publication and bee finish follow the execution runbook.
Consult addendum — 2026-10-09 — precise names from the added user question

Read the task note added during this exploration, including the user's decision: “I think it makes sense for a user to own the process rather than the daemon. That way they are decoupled ... listen to what the daemon is saying without necessarily tearing it down if you happen to put in a bad bit of code.”

External listener process ownership is therefore settled user direction, not an unresolved daemon-versus-external hosting choice. The report's “who starts it” question is narrowed to the user's chosen invocation/service-manager arrangement and restart policy. No Colony-managed listener host is recommended. Remaining assessment replay/sleep/evidence decisions still need explicit semantics.

Direct answers to the three candidate names:
- “Request created”: useful, but native submission and daemon discovery are different facts. Bee producer.ts:112–129 creates the spawn in Beads even while the daemon is down/asleep. Colony dispatch.ts:104–114 can authoritatively emit request.observed when it first persists that request. Do not name that delayed observation request.created. A true creation feed needs a Beads/Bee-owned durable source/ingestion contract, including creations stopped before Colony ever sees them. Sending a best-effort socket notification from Bee would miss precisely the offline case. For the next Colony-only catalogue, prefer request.observed; retain native creation time separately.
- “Bee launched”: useful, but prefer an attempt-qualified name. attempt.reserved means capacity/launch authority committed; attempt.started means a harness actually started. Supervisor start or execution permission alone does not establish the latter. Both belong to a particular attemptId under a requestId. Automatic retries produce new attempts for the same request/identity; bee retry creates a different request. If the desired UI is merely “launch is underway,” reservation is the cheaper reliable milestone; if it means “harness started,” preserve and validate start evidence as described in the catalogue.
- “Bee alive”: useful for a live UI, but not a timeless lifecycle fact and not equivalent to output activity. Proposed LATER attempt.liveness_observed has {requestId,attemptId,execution:live|stopped,observedAt}, emitted only when an awake Colony performs and durably records an ownership-verified observation through processes.ts:127–145. A nonmatching/missing/unverifiable ownership error must not be converted to stopped. In that existing function, live can include a pending supervisor before a harness is proven started; either keep that precise execution meaning or add a distinct, proven harness observation before using a “bee alive” label. This is not currently a public event.
  For change notifications, emit changed liveness observations and use a supported fresh inspection query when the consumer needs current truth. If a consumer specifically needs periodic liveness samples, choose an explicit bounded cadence and retain observedAt; this becomes a higher-volume observation feed, not an automatic heartbeat in the durable catalogue. No cadence or timeout policy is approved here. Current colony inspect is retained checkpoint evidence, so fresh public ownership-verified inspection is still a proposed extension. A stale last-live event does not prove continued life; no new event while asleep/disconnected does not prove death. attempt.output_observed separately means stdout changed, not that an agent is making useful progress.

This addendum addresses the added user question and narrows the one hosting question without changing the prioritized next set, source authority, write scope or original advice history.

description:

You are the Hive librarian: curator of architectural intent, not a directory index. Keep the architecture guidance useful to implementing agents, help resolve unclear designs, and identify where that guidance repeatedly fails them.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Obtain the task bead if one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- With explicit editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the recurring questions, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or unresolved decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Prune stale guidance rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Within authorized curation:

1. Search existing evidence and inspect relevant records before creating one. Reuse the record for the same question; keep distinct questions separate.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Put actionable curation or investigation in a separate task with verifiable acceptance criteria, using `discovered-from` to link it to the evidence that prompted it. Follow the root runbook for that work; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements for every authorized mutation. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish and report record IDs and publication status. Report access or synchronization failures without bypassing them.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates; leave unknowns explicit:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the implementing agent understood; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. Consult and review leave their targets unchanged; only linked delivery-task reporting and completion are authorized without curation scope.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

- **Verdict** — aligned, or not aligned.

- **Confirmed** — briefly, what is aligned.
- **Not verified** — anything you could not check, and why.

## Constraints

- Never fix code: report findings only.

You are the Hive librarian: curator of architectural intent, not a directory index. Keep the architecture guidance useful to implementing agents, help resolve unclear designs, and identify where that guidance repeatedly fails them.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Obtain the task bead if one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- With explicit editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the recurring questions, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or unresolved decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Prune stale guidance rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Within authorized curation:

1. Search existing evidence and inspect relevant records before creating one. Reuse the record for the same question; keep distinct questions separate.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Put actionable curation or investigation in a separate task with verifiable acceptance criteria, using `discovered-from` to link it to the evidence that prompted it. Follow the root runbook for that work; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements for every authorized mutation. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish and report record IDs and publication status. Report access or synchronization failures without bypassing them.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates; leave unknowns explicit:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the implementing agent understood; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. Consult and review leave their targets unchanged; only linked delivery-task reporting and completion are authorized without curation scope.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

title: Architecture evidence: Honeycomb repository-local config seam
description:
- **architectural-friction** — 2026-10-10; topic key `honeycomb.repository-local-config`; hv-yzqf5.1 asks how canonical repository-local configuration should extend the existing loading/resolution seam, particularly optional values, copy defaults, effective-command validation and explain provenance.
- **Interpretation** — The originating request, as summarized in hv-yzqf5 (not a verbatim user transcript), wants canonical-root `honeycomb.toml`, reused applicable schema shapes, no selectors, and explicit local overrides over resolved global configuration. Existing ConfigService already separates synchronous file loading from pure resolution; ProjectConfig is both an exact global entry and the copy/pool caller shape. The difficult cases are defaults that destroy omission information, command requirements needing another layer, and avoiding false exact-project provenance for local-only configuration.
- **Resolution** — Librarian recommendation, not yet accepted: use `read(canonicalRoot): TreesConfig`; commands retain Git discovery and pass the existing canonical root to the live adapter. Represent the parsed local file separately as a root/path plus optional patch; keep matching and merging in domain/config.ts. Reuse strict project option shapes without selectors or local defaults. Apply local policy last, merge finish field-by-field, replace copy arrays including [], preserve false, and continue serving an effective ProjectConfig to copy/pool consumers. Preserve the global exact entry separately for public explain.project; add local-file attribution and distinguish local command/hook sources. For local replacement copy lists, use local default, inherited exact-project default, then copy; explicit entry modes win. Proposed resolved-layer semantics leave inherited global copy entries unchanged when local copy is absent. Retain existing global-file validation; validate local setup requirements against the combined command before lifecycle mutations. A local file must not require its own command if the global exact entry or matching rule supplies one.
- **Guidance gap** — Existing canonical identity and injected IO ownership are clear. Local overlay behavior is new. The supplied request does not explicitly settle whether changing only local copy_mode_default should rewrite modes of inherited global entries, or whether a local command should make an otherwise-invalid global project valid. Above are conservative proposals based on final overlay over an already-resolved, valid global configuration, not established policy.
- **Action/outcome** — Consultation delivered on hv-yzqf5.1; implementation acceptance and testing remain pending on hv-yzqf5. Coordinator should record accepted edge semantics in the implementation design, or return a different intended behavior to this thread. If inherited entry modes must be reinterpreted, retain optional per-entry mode until final materialization; never infer omission from mode equalling the old default. If global setup may rely on a local command, selected-root command validation must move after composition while retaining strict shape checks. No source/docs edits or test suites performed by librarian; this is a design consultation, not a final implementation review. Next useful evidence: final diff, focused precedence/default/validation cases and real invocation from a feature checkout with conflicting local files, plus parent-required validation.

Read docs/PHILOSOPHY.md, docs/architecture.md (Honeycomb execution/state and authority), GLOSSARY.md canonical terms, lib/honeycomb/AGENTS.md and devflow/specs/git-worktrees.md.
